title: Checkpoint restore silently drops the per-entry `recon` score and never restores the store-level `gate_theta`, contradicting docs/04_CONTRACT.md's own claim that these were the fix for two of the four checkpoint omissions that 'each disarmed a live mechanism at the run boundary'
failure: docs/04_CONTRACT.md's MEM section states as settled fact: "Checkpointed additions: prob, recon, nsrc_max, gate_theta -- four omissions that each disarmed a live mechanism at the run boundary." Of those four, `prob` and `nsrc_max` are genuinely restored per-row/store (memory/api.py:219, :244); `recon` and `gate_theta` are not restored anywhere in the file. `_restore_by_block`'s per-row loop (lines 204-232) reads r["key"]/tok/src/pos/ctx/own/active/prob/use/last/born from the blob but never reads a `recon` (or `selfcon`) field, and neither `open_store` nor `_restore_by_block` ever assigns `store.gate_theta` from the blob -- it is left at `Store.__init__`'s literal default of 0.0 regardless of what a checkpoint recorded. Reproduced directly: constructed a store via `open_store`, then called `_restore_by_block` with a synthetic blob row carrying `selfcon=0.87, recon=0.42` and a top-level `gate_theta=0.35`. After restore: `store.selfcon[0] == 0.0` (not 0.87), `store.recon[0] == 0.0` (not 0.42), and `store.gate_theta == 0.0` (not 0.35). `gate_theta` is the adaptive write-admission floor and `recon` is the reconstruction/verification score EVAL's `verification_fit`/`wrongness_probe` are specified against; both silently reset at every resume boundary -- the boundary goal B's every forgetting number is measured across.
evidence: docs/04_CONTRACT.md, MEM section: "Checkpointed additions: prob, recon, nsrc_max, gate_theta -- four omissions that each disarmed a live mechanism at the run boundary." memory/api.py:204-232 (`_restore_by_block`'s per-row loop) restores tok/src/pos/ctx/own/active/prob/use/last/born only -- no `recon` or `selfcon` key is ever read from `r`. `grep -n gate_theta src/memory/api.py` finds it only in `Store.__init__`'s literal default (`self.gate_theta = 0.0`) and in `open_store`'s Gate arithmetic docstring text -- never assigned from `restored`/`blob`. Measured via the repo's own open_store/_restore_by_block: restoring a row with selfcon=0.87/recon=0.42 and a blob-level gate_theta=0.35 leaves store.selfcon[0]=0.0, store.recon[0]=0.0, store.gate_theta=0.0 after restore.
fix: In `_restore_by_block`'s per-row loop, add `store.recon[free] = float(r.get("recon", 0.0))` and `store.selfcon[free] = float(r.get("selfcon", 0.0))` alongside the other per-row restores; in `open_store` or `_restore_by_block`, restore `store.gate_theta = float(blob.get("gate_theta", 0.0))` from the top-level blob the way `tick`/`n_written`/`nsrc_max` already are (lines 240-244). (state_dict, the save-side counterpart, is still a stub, so this needs to land together with that entry point's own write-side of prob/recon/gate_theta for the round trip to hold.)

title: open_store's mem.key_depth Gate reports FIRED whenever MEM_KEY_DEPTH>0 on the transformer arm, even though LM.encode structurally ignores n_layers and can never truncate the key path
failure: MEM_KEY_SRC=model, LM_ARCH=transformer, MEM_KEY_DEPTH=3 (any run that wants the memory-key depth cut). Reproduced: `open_store(...)` returns `store.gates == (Gate('mem.key_depth', True, 3, 0),)`, and `Gate.line()` prints 'Gate mem.key_depth: FIRED (3 vs 0)'. But lm/api.py::encode's body (lines 436-457) never references its own `n_layers` parameter -- verified separately that `encode(cfg, m, x, n_layers=1)` and `encode(cfg, m, x)` return byte-identical tensors -- so the truncation this Gate claims happened cannot execute on ANY call in ANY run of the current tree; it is not merely unfired this session, it is unbuildable. A report reading this Gate concludes the memory-key path is paying for a shallow (3-layer) encode when it is structurally still paying for the full stack every time, which is exactly the cost lm/api.py's own docstring (around line 410) says the mechanism exists to avoid. This is the three-state collapse spine/gate.py exists to prevent, produced by one package's Gate (MEM) trusting a config predicate instead of the sibling package's (LM) actual capability -- a two-package interaction neither side's own tests can see, because MEM never imports LM and evaluates the gate from Config alone.
evidence: memory/api.py:179 `Gate("mem.key_depth", int(mem.key_depth) > 0, int(mem.key_depth), 0)` `if str(mem.key_src) == "model" and str(lm_kind) == "transformer" else ...`. lm/api.py:436 `def encode(lm: Config, model, x, *, n_layers=None, extra=None):` with a body (lm/api.py:449-457) that computes `e`, `h` and returns `h` with no read of `n_layers` anywhere -- the same underlying gap round 1 already filed against lm/api.py's `encode` ('encode accepts n_layers and never uses it'), here observed instead through MEM's own Gate, in an entry point (open_store) neither round examined. spine/gate.py's own docstring: 'fired=False, reachable=True means the mechanism ran and its condition was not met... reachable=False means the condition CANNOT be met on this configuration' -- MEM_KEY_DEPTH>0 on the transformer arm is exactly that second case today, and the Gate reports the first. Verified live: `python3 -c "...open_store(...).gates..."` printed `Gate mem.key_depth: FIRED (3 vs 0)`.
fix: Until LM.encode's n_layers is wired up (the already-filed defect), open_store's Gate must not claim FIRED for this configuration: report it `reachable=False` with a reason naming that LM.encode does not yet implement the cut, or thread a capability flag from LM through the wire so MEM can tell 'the sibling package can do this' from 'the operator asked for it'. Once encode() actually truncates, the existing predicate becomes correct and this repair is removable.

title: open_store's LEVERS READ line names 14 levers; the body reads 3 of them, and the other 10 (beyond the package-documented owners/wire exception) are never read anywhere in the file
failure: The docstring at line 137-138 declares "LEVERS READ: quota, owners, key_src, key_win, key_depth, evict, probation_frac, src_share, verify, recon_hid, recon_tok, topk, write_mode, write_gate" -- fourteen levers. The body (lines 142-186) reads only `mem.quota` (line 146), `mem.key_src` and `mem.key_depth` (lines 179-182). `owners` is separately and correctly reconciled by this package's own module docstring ("the 25th lever and this package's own code never reads it -- spine/assemble.py reads it to compute two of those three wires"), so it is not itself a defect. But `key_win`, `evict`, `probation_frac`, `src_share`, `verify`, `recon_hid`, `recon_tok`, `topk`, `write_mode` and `write_gate` have no such carve-out and are simply never referenced anywhere in src/memory/api.py -- they are consumed only by `write`/`read`/`blend`/`maintain`/`judge`, all of which are still-unimplemented stubs. An operator reading open_store's frozen contract to learn what this call consumes is told ten levers are read that are not, in the same shape round1 already flagged on fabric.build and tok.build_vocabulary.
evidence: memory/api.py:137-138 declares the 14-lever list; body at :142-186 reads `mem.quota`, `mem.key_src`, `mem.key_depth` and the three wires `mem.d_capacity`/`mem.d_owner_blocks`/`mem.d_source_slots`. `grep -n "mem\.\(evict\|probation_frac\|src_share\|verify\|recon_hid\|recon_tok\|topk\|write_mode\|write_gate\|key_win\)\b" src/memory/api.py` returns nothing.
fix: Trim open_store's LEVERS READ line to "quota, key_src, key_depth" (plus the owners exception already explained in the module docstring), and leave the other ten declared on the entry points that actually consume them (write, read, maintain, judge) once those bodies land.
